objective: v1.2 small-capital construction: can the unchanged v1.2 M0_U3000 book run in a $50,000 Alpaca account (fractional DAY-order longs, whole-share ETB shorts) and keep >= 0.80 of the full $1M account's recent Sharpe (F1 excess over BIL, F2 information ratio over SPY), with V2 feasibility, by concentrating to the top-K names per side (R1, R1B) or by dropping the short stock leg (R3)?

cost_table.base_cost_bps: make_cost_fn('close') at the tier's own notional (half-spread from D4 15:45 NBBO samples, square-root impact, 0.5 bp fees); borrow 0 bp ETB
cost_table.stress_cost_bps: 2x trading cost on the same path plus 25 bp borrow on short notional

sources.core_claim: Alpaca fractional orders are supported for market, limit, stop and stop limit orders with time in force Day only, so fractional longs cannot use the opening or closing auction (opg/cls).
sources.project_applicability: Forces the small-capital book to trade its fractional long leg with DAY orders; the contract therefore trades the whole book as DAY orders around 15:50 ET.
sources.reflection: Documentation, not a fill study; says nothing about fill quality at 15:50.

sources.core_claim: Alpaca does not support short sales in fractional orders, so every short position must be a whole number of shares.
sources.project_applicability: The reason the 1,784-name v1.2 short leg rounds to zero shares for most names at $50,000 (T-71) and the reason for the top-K concentration.

sources.core_claim: Alpaca paper trading matches every order against the current NBBO (the same page states random partial fills 10% of the time and no NBBO depth check), so paper cannot reproduce auction fills.
sources.project_applicability: A 15:50 DAY-order book is executed the same way on paper and live (quote-based), unlike auction orders; the 10-15 paper account can test the chosen execution path.
sources.reflection: Paper ignores depth and borrow fees; partial fills are random, not market-driven.

sources.core_claim: Alpaca requires at least $2,000 of account equity to trade on margin or sell short.
sources.project_applicability: Not binding at the $25,000-$100,000 tiers of this contract; recorded so the minimum-capital answer is complete.

sources.core_claim: Alpaca offers more than 5,000 easy-to-borrow securities approved for locates with zero fees, so ETB shorts carry no borrow fee.
sources.project_applicability: Main borrow cost 0 bp for the ETB-restricted short leg (v1.2 convention), 25 bp sensitivity kept.
sources.reflection: ETB status changes daily; our ETB proxy (D7, precision 0.985) is not the broker list.

sources.core_claim: Blitz, Baltussen and van Vliet (Financial Analysts Journal 76(4), 2020): most factor value comes from the long legs, long legs diversify more than short legs, and short-leg performance is generally subsumed by the long legs.
sources.project_applicability: Basis of candidate R3 (drop the short stock leg, hedge its beta with SPY); R1 must beat R3 to justify whole-share shorts at small capital.
sources.reflection: Abstract only; factor portfolios, not our composite; ignores short-implementation costs that would favour R3 further.

sources.core_claim: Clarke, de Silva and Thorley (Financial Analysts Journal 58(5), 2002): constraints on short positions and turnover are common and materially restrictive; the generalized fundamental law splits performance into forecast skill and constraint noise (transfer coefficient).
sources.project_applicability: Frames the expected Sharpe loss of the whole-share and concentration constraints; measured here with return-based retention and tracking error, not weight correlation (I-20261005-01 probe: weight correlation 0.999 is uninformative).
sources.reflection: Abstract only; the 0.73 / 0.3 transfer coefficients come from press coverage, not the paper text read here.

sources.core_claim: Long-short extension (130/30-type) portfolios relax the long-only constraint; the benefit depends on how much shorting is allowed (FAJ 64(1), 2008, abstract).
sources.project_applicability: F2 is a SPY core plus overlay; index-relative underweights are the extension view of its short leg.
sources.reflection: Index-relative underweights need point-in-time index weights we do not have; recorded as not done.

sources.core_claim: Sparse index tracking by majorization-minimization selects names and weights jointly with tracking comparable to or better than benchmarks at far lower run time (IEEE TSP 66(1), 2018, abstract and introduction).
sources.project_applicability: Named follow-up if R1 fails retention: a sparse tracking optimizer instead of a top-K cut.
sources.reflection: GPL R package; long-only index tracking; would need a re-implementation for long-short.

sources.core_claim: Median extension strategies beat median long-only strategies on rolling three-year net returns in eVestment data (NEPC, April 2025).
sources.project_applicability: Industry context for keeping a short leg; not small-account evidence.
sources.reflection: Consultant survey, survivorship and selection unknown.

sources.core_claim: PyPortfolioOpt's DiscreteAllocation rounds continuous weights to whole shares greedily or by integer programming and splits long and short books before allocating.
sources.project_applicability: Same split as R1 (shorts rounded on their own); confirms the two-step approach is the common open-source practice.
sources.reflection: Does not select names, so it does not solve sub-one-share short targets.

sources.core_claim: Whole-share rounding zeroes small weights and creates tracking error; the vendor says the problem binds below about $50,000 for US large-cap accounts.
sources.project_applicability: Order of magnitude consistent with T-71; vendor claim, not used as evidence.

hypothesis.statement: Concentrating each side of the v1.2 book to its top-K names (K* = the largest K that is whole-share feasible at $50,000) keeps at least 0.80 of the full account's recent Sharpe, because the target weights are concentrated in the largest names and the dropped tail carries little of the composite's edge.
hypothesis.failure_mode: The edge sits in the many small positions (breadth), so retention falls below 0.80; or the K boundary churns and costs eat the edge; or the short leg adds nothing over R3.
hypothesis.measurement: Sharpe retention vs the $1M A1 account in the recent window 2024-01-08..2026-09-15 (stress 2017-10-02..2023-08-31 reported), V2 feasibility per session, tracking error vs the full account, 20-seed random-name placebo, 2x cost, 36-series DSR.
hypothesis.stop_pivot: No deployable config at $50,000: report the minimum tier ($100,000 or above), keep the ETF pilot as the live path, and the next step is a sparse tracking optimizer or exact whole-share MILP (not a refutation of v1.2).

decision.reason: Preregistered 2026-10-06 01:07 lead round before any small-capital return series.
decision.next_iteration_suggestion: Production target generator for the small account and a 10-15 paper start if a config is deployable and the owner approves the account.
